_comment: Every thing that decides whether an output is correct -- grader, scorer, equivalence check, data loader -- with a name, what_it_decides, a positive_test proving it accepts a known-correct input, and a negative_test proving it rejects a known-wrong one. requires_tools lists anything genuinely external (a closed-book run that fell back to a synthetic corpus passed every gate and meant nothing; the data-loader fingerprint catches that). A grader that cannot run must raise, never return a negative verdict -- the *_blocked_here tests assert the real backbones raise BlockedException in this CPU sandbox rather than fabricating a score. Subprocess invocations inside the tests use sys.executable (never bare python). Schema validated by tests/test_instruments.py. If nothing here judged an output we would say so with not_applicable and a reason; this reproduction has nine instruments, so not_applicable does not apply.

instruments.name: data_loader
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether the paper's own model+dataset is loaded (vs a synthetic fallback) for the model arms. load_model_activations raises BlockedException when there is no CUDA and/or no HF_TOKEN, so a blocked arm is reported rather than silently substituted. A closed-book run that fell back to a synthetic corpus produced seven arms at chance level (perplexity 65 on a 65-token vocabulary) and passed every gate; this loader is the instrument that prevents that -- it must NOT fall back to synthetic data. The positive test is a fingerprint analog on the synthetic Gaussian (PSD Sigma_XX, Sigma_XZ in Im(Sigma_XX)); the real-load path additionally asserts DATA_FINGERPRINTS[model_id] (size/vocab/checksum) when CUDA+HF_TOKEN are present (not reachable in this CPU sandbox).

instruments.name: judge_cs
instruments.what_it_decides: The per-text concept-relevance score 0-10, computed by argmax over the '0'..'10' token probabilities of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. This is the LLM-judge concept score the claims evaluate. The positive test proves the argmax scoring logic maps peaked logits to the right integer (7.0); the negative test proves a different peak yields a different score (1.0), so it is not a constant stub, and the *_blocked_here test proves the real backbone raises BlockedException here rather than fabricating a score.

instruments.name: clip_cs
instruments.what_it_decides: The image concept-relevance score: cosine similarity x100 between a steered image and the concept text under CLIP. The positive test proves the x100 scale (sim 1.0 => 100.0); the negative test proves the real backbone raises BlockedException in this sandbox rather than fabricating a number. Backbone gap G11: the paper does not pin a CLIP backbone; we default to openai/clip-vit-base-patch32.

instruments.name: fid
instruments.what_it_decides: The Frechet Inception Distance between the steered and vanilla image sets -- a distributional distance, so identical statistics give ~0 and disjoint means give a large value. The positive test asserts identical stats => FID ~ 0; the negative test asserts disjoint means => large FID (discriminating, not a rubber stamp) and the *_blocked_here test asserts the real estimator raises BlockedException here.

instruments.name: detoxify_score
instruments.what_it_decides: The mean Detoxify 'original' toxicity probability over generated continuations (RealToxicityPrompts). The positive test proves the mean aggregation ([0.9,0.8] => 0.85); the negative test proves an empty success set raises (a grader that cannot run must raise, never return a negative verdict) and the *_blocked_here test proves the real model raises BlockedException here.

instruments.name: armorm_score
instruments.what_it_decides: The ArmoRM-Llama3-8B helpfulness attribute over continuations. The positive test proves the mean aggregation ([0.4,0.6] => 0.5); the negative test proves the real backbone raises BlockedException here rather than fabricating a score.

instruments.name: bertscore_mmlu
instruments.what_it_decides: BERTScore Precision/F1 between MMLU generations and references. The positive test proves identical strings => 1.0; the negative test proves an empty input raises (no silent 0.0) and the *_blocked_here test proves the real backbone raises BlockedException here.

instruments.name: closed_form_invariants
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether the affine maps satisfy the paper's covariance constraints (Eqs. 5/13/19) and minimal-disturbance on synthetic Gaussian data, and the erasure special case MidSteer==LEACE (paper/main.tex:461). This is the closed-form invariant checker for claims C1-C3 -- the CPU-reachable correctness evidence. The positive tests assert ||A Sxz||<1e-9 (C1), the switch flips the sign of the covariance (C2), MidSteer matches the target covariance (C3), and the erasure special case equals LEACE; experiments/run_e1_synth.py runs the full predicate incl. minimal-disturbance over the feasible perturbation family and the vanilla special case. The negative tests are the mutation suite: deliberate defects (sign slip / broken bias / broken Welford) flip these assertions, so the named test nodes must fail.

instruments.name: evaluate_claims
instruments.what_it_decides: The pass/fail/blocked verdict per claim, written to claims_result.json by the WORKFLOW's numbers gate, evaluated against measured.json + results/e1_synth.json per the claims.json evaluation_rule. A blocked metric is never a silent pass; a grader that cannot run (malformed/empty claims or measured) raises rather than emitting a verdict; a metric nothing measures is BLOCKED, not a rounding error. The positive test proves a satisfied ordering passes; the negative tests prove a violated ordering fails, a blocked metric is blocked, an empty claims table raises, an empty measured table raises, and an unmeasured metric is blocked.
instruments.produces: claims_result.json (workflow artifact; the agent's own check writes selfcheck.json, a different filename)

not_applicable.reason: This reproduction has nine output-deciding instruments (one data loader, six eval-metric scorers, one closed-form invariant checker, one claims evaluator), so the not_applicable case (nothing here judges an output) does not apply. not_applicable is reserved for a reproduction where no instrument judges correctness; here every arm's measured number is produced or blocked by one of the listed instruments.
